identity.north_star: Bind one exact hardware artifact and revision through engineering evidence, deterministic verification, physical evidence, and explicit human authority without conflating those evidence classes.
native_lane: hardware engineering evidence and revision-bound validation
not_trying_to_be: replacement for KiCad Altium Cadence or Flux

priority_stack.goal: Complete one revision-bound physical evidence chain from independent review through evidence closure.
Keep the merged artifact-first Review/Compare/Verify/Bring-up shell closed unless a concrete usability, evaluator, or source-bound competitor gap reopens it.
Use HS where hardware physical-agent release-assurance or consequential-authority fit is intrinsic.

Add authoring, routing, parts intelligence, 3D and real-time collaboration as layers that PRODUCE REVIEWABLE CANDIDATES. Every change flows through diff, retention and staged review; none grants authority.

route_specific_integrations.guard: must be HS-native source-bound and useful to a real workflow or route

competitor_driven_improvement.guard: gap must be native and evidence-backed

proposal_capability_expansion.decision_basis: source-bound competitor gap review: authoring, routing, parts, 3D and live collaboration are table stakes in Flux, AllSpice, Altium 365 and Quilter-class products
rules: every capability emits a candidate that is reviewed through the existing staged review before it can become a revision
no capability can change an authority, release, fabrication or power-on state
integrate mature engines (KiCad, kicad-cli, FreeRouting, distributor APIs) instead of rebuilding them
never invent data: parts, availability and provenance are filled only from the design or a named provider with as_of
a generic AI/EDA feature race stays off; each addition must be native to the evidence and review model

backend.kicad_edit_operations: kicad_edit.py: deterministic move, rotate, set_property, set_flag, add_label, set_track_width and delete over retained bytes
backend.candidate_proposals: project_candidates.py: edits or an autoroute become a pending staged review with a structural diff and optional DRC/ERC counts
backend.routing_candidates: routing_engine.py: FreeRouting through KiCad's pcbnew, behind a capability probe and a copper-only result guard
backend.parts_intelligence: parts_intel.py: BOM from the design's own properties, enrichment opt-in with source and as_of
backend.model3d_viewer: model3d.py: GLB from retained PCB bytes via kicad-cli, cached by hash
backend.live_events_and_presence: project_events.py and project_presence.py: change stream and ephemeral presence, information only
backend.review_packet: review_packet.py and GET /v1/projects/{id}/review-packet: a hash-bound, read-only, deterministic JSON/Markdown packet of one revision (retained file hashes, findings, proposals with decisions, discussion) with an explicit not-established section and best-effort credential and path redaction; include_text=false builds the version for sharing with every user-written field left out
backend.retained_file_bytes: GET /revisions/{rev}/artifacts/{kind}/file: exact retained bytes with ETag and revalidation, so a viewer shows the file that was hashed
backend.assembly_plan: assembly_plan.py and GET /v1/projects/{id}/revisions/{rev}/assembly-plan (+ /board.glb): an ordered build sequence read from the retained board: real part positions and outlines, typical heights with their basis, pin 1, connector pins and nets, suggested continuity checks, parts the design marks do-not-populate reported as not fitted. A view of retained bytes; heights and order are labelled estimates
backend.device_plan: device_plan.py, device_api.py and data/device_modules.json: a whole-gadget assembly plan (modules, wires pin to pin, a proposed case, ordered steps) from a spec, with a module library whose every figure names its source or is marked typical (ESP32-DevKitC V4 from Espressif's drawing and pin tables and the WROOM-32E datasheet; the common SSD1306 OLED module). Wiring is checked against pin roles and as nets. Stateless, report-only
backend.salvage_plan: salvage_plan.py and GET /revisions/{rev}/salvage-plan: the build sequence run the other way over a retained board: a safety step, removal order, and a verdict with its rule for each part (worth taking, test first, read the marking, cheap to buy new, leave it). Names a chip only as far as the board file does; never calls a part good; states that it needs the board's file. Report-only

delivered.frontend: evidence workspace: Parts tab (find a part on the drawing), 3D tab, presence and live threads, a docked Edit toolbar with a live draft preview, Proposals tab with preview, marked changes and operator-gated accept/reject, faint copper fills
not_yet_verified: live FreeRouting run: no jar was installed where this was built; the guard was exercised with fake engines and a real pcbnew round-trip only
parts availability from a real distributor provider: only the offline catalog and an opt-in jlcsearch provider exist
delivered.independent_review: Codex adversarial reviews on 2026-10-06 and 2026-10-07 found and drove fixes for: orphan cleanup through a symlinked ancestor, subprocess groups surviving an exited leader, a read-only preview that could repair a damaged store, and drafts, selections and previews matched by file kind or name instead of full path. Each fix has a regression test shown to fail on the old behaviour.
delivered.frontend_comparison: Compare: Before, Swipe and Difference views of two retained revisions, with a shared camera, drawn from the hash-verified files; measured so identical files show under 0.3% differing pixels
delivered.independent_review_review_packet: Codex adversarial review ran 21 further rounds on 2026-10-07 on the packet and comparison viewer; each real finding was reproduced, fixed and covered by a regression test (credential-name detection by component words, order-independent size limits, YAML secret blocks across line endings, list markers, anchors, project id and every user-written field omitted from the shared version). One finding was declined: error responses echo the caller's own project id to the caller.
delivered.frontend_assembly: Evidence workspace Assemble tab: parts descend onto outlines of their real positions on the KiCad-exported board in the plan's order, with play, step, slider and keys; stand-in shapes are labelled
delivered.independent_review_assembly: Codex found and drove fixes for: parts marked dnp being instructed, a 13 s quadratic check generator, arc outlines bounded by their ends, duplicate references collapsing in the viewer, a leaked WebGL context when the tab was left mid-load, generated ids colliding with real references, and all-dnp boards hiding what was left off. The outline maths is compared with KiCad's own geometry after KiCad turns and flips parts.
not_yet_verified_assembly: off-board parts (screens, batteries, cases) are not drawn: only the retained board's parts; real component models need kicad-packages3d; 'connect A to B' wire animation between modules is not built
delivered.frontend_device: Engineering > Build a device: parts hover apart, the board drops into the case, each wire grows from pin to pin with both pins named, the display, lid and USB follow; wiring findings with their basis, shopping list, what to measure before printing, links to every source, and an editable spec to see what the checks say about wrong wiring
delivered.independent_review_device: Codex data-truth review found no mismatch with the cited sources; it found and drove fixes for: reset and flash pins passing as harmless when wired to the display's power or ground, a case sized from the board alone, a request limit applied after buffering, malformed JSON values reaching a 500, wires not following a moving display, supply bridges formed by two individually fine wires, and a rejected wire hiding a bridge
not_yet_verified_device: the case has not been printed or test-fitted: its numbers are typical, not measured
a battery needs a charger and regulator module, not yet in the library
only two module types exist; other ESP32 boards and displays differ in size and pin order
delivered.frontend_salvage: Assemble tab 'Take apart': parts lift off in order, coloured by verdict, removed parts leave their outline, with verdict chip, hazards, counts and the plan's limits
not_yet_verified_salvage: boards with no file cannot be planned from: there is no photo or marking capture path into the 3D view
the take-apart code had no independent Codex review (its quota ran out); it was reviewed by hand and the chip-identification rule tightened
